en.headline: No special road closures near Cape Collinson today, government says
en.dek: A spokesman dismissed online claims that hearses and coaches would be barred from the Chai Wan crematorium area on Sunday morning.
body: The government said there are no special traffic control measures around Cape Collinson Crematorium in Chai Wan today, after posts circulated online claiming roads would be closed and hearses and coaches barred from entering on Sunday morning.

A government spokesman said on Saturday evening that vehicles with booked cremation services may enter and leave the crematorium in an orderly way, following on-site directions from police and Food and Environmental Hygiene Department staff.

The clarification was issued as the state funeral cortege for former chief executive Tung Chee-hwa was scheduled to leave North Point after a 9am memorial and proceed later to the Chai Wan crematorium. Officials had already announced separate, limited traffic measures in North Point and Quarry Bay for the funeral movement.
Drivers heading to booked services at Cape Collinson were advised to allow extra time and follow staff instructions at the site, rather than assume a full road closure.

zh.headline: 政府澄清哥連臣角今日沒有特別封路
zh.dek: 發言人否認網傳周日早上禁止靈車及旅遊巴士進入柴灣火葬場一帶的說法。
body: 政府表示，今日哥連臣角火葬場附近一帶並沒有特別交通管制措施。早前網上流傳火葬場周日早上會封路，禁止所有靈車及旅遊巴士進入。
政府發言人周六晚上澄清，已預約火化服務的車輛，可按現場警方及食物環境衞生署職員的安排和指示，有序進出火葬場。
當局作出澄清之際，正值前行政長官董建華國葬儀式於北角舉行，公祭後靈車稍後前往柴灣火葬場。運輸署早前已就北角及鰭魚涌一帶的殮儀車隊公布獨立的有限度交通措施。
當局提醒前往哥連臣角已預約服務的司機預留時間，並聽從現場人員指示，不必假設道路全面封閉。
